reuse.why: All five midpoint sites now call getExpectedScheduleAmount and the tolerance comes from the existing getApproxNumberThreshold, but getScheduledAmount keeps its own null/number dispatch instead of delegating.

duplication.why: The repeated midpoint dispatches are removed; the remaining overlap is getScheduledAmount re-deciding the null/number/range dispatch that getExpectedScheduleAmount owns.

placement.why: The rule sits in shared/schedules beside getScheduledAmount and is consumed by server, forecast, budget-template and API model layers.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule and the API field, with tests and release notes; several comments and a release note were left describing the superseded 'furthest from zero' rule.

maintainability.why: One definition for most paths, but getScheduledAmount (used by the desktop client) ignores the approximate rule and stale comments contradict the final lowest-value rule.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getScheduledAmount in shared/schedules.ts keeps its own null/number handling and never calls getExpectedScheduleAmount, so its desktop-client callers skip the approximate-amount rule.

disguised_duplication.where: getScheduledAmount's residual dispatch is an open parallel path, not a disguised copy.

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedScheduleAmount gained an op parameter and an isapprox branch (both legitimate for the rule); getScheduledAmount bypasses it, re-implementing the null/number dispatch and omitting the approximate case.
